text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: Institutional records offices file ordinary paperwork by accession number, retention class, and custodian. Access is logged. Periodic audits match the index to storage.

2) What occurred: The actor generated a coordinated scheduling document listing multiple named accounts with a shared date field for rent adjustments. A second document allocated neighborhood segments to each named account, using a "coverage" field to assign exclusive zones. A third document recorded an enforcement clause naming a target account that applied a discount below the group rate, followed by a penalty entry in a "compliance" field. The actor then transmitted scheduling updates through an ephemeral chat channel, deleting the original draft after transmission. A summary message in that channel referenced "alignment" without stating pricing terms explicitly.

3) Materials/access observed: The scheduling document resided in a shared drive folder with a retention class of "project" and no custodian assignment. The neighborhood allocation file used a spreadsheet with a column titled "Territory." The enforcement record appeared as a dated entry in a log file with an "action" field. The chat channel was a self-destructing messaging group, and the original draft was removed within one business day. Access logs showed the actor creating the shared drive folder and granting edit rights to the named accounts.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Synchronized date values across independent named accounts in a shared document. A coverage/territory assignment column mapping accounts to non-overlapping geographic zones. A compliance field containing penalty language tied to a discount event. Use of ephemeral messaging to discuss timing without stating monetary terms. Draft file deletion immediately after transmission. Absence of a custodian on the shared folder. These artifacts, viewed in sequence, constitute a pattern of coordinated conduct detectable through temporal correlation and field-content analysis.
